chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: May wudu be performed from the leftover water of a menstruating woman? He said: “No.”

So the sound approach regarding these reports is what he explained in the earlier reports, and that is: if the woman is not trusted, then performing wudu with her leftover water is not permissible. It is also possible that what is meant by them is a kind of recommendation, and that indicates this.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation or preferred practice in law
key_terms.بِسُؤْرِهَا: with her leftover water after drinking or use
key_terms.فَضْلِ الْحَائِضِ: the leftover water remaining after a menstruating woman has used it
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trusted regarding purity and avoidance of contamination

ai.seo_question: Can wudu be performed with the leftover water of a menstruating woman?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on performing wudu with the leftover water of a menstruating woman. Its reconciliation explains that the prohibition applies when she is not trusted, while the reports may also be understood as indicating a matter of recommendation rather than absolute prohibition.
